📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith.

In a recent development, I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Chelsea’s former techincal director Michael Emenalo has taken up an advisory role at Leicester City.

The Athletic reports that the Nigerian, who was with the Blues for five and a half years, is part of a team of consultants that is helping the Foxes with their future planning.

The fallen giants are now in League One after back-to-back relegations from the Premier League and the Championship, and the 2016 top-flight champions right now sit 11th in the third tier.

Russell Martin, the ex-Southampton and Rangers manager, is the man tasked with taking the east Midlands side back into the second division, but financial restraints have hindered their progress.

Now, they have turned to Emenalo and his team of Deloitte consultants to help them strategise for the coming months.

Emenalo, who was a left-back in his playing days, was most recently the ‘chief football executive’ for the entire Saudi Pro League, taking up the position in July 2023.

He departed in the summer of 2026 after three years in the post, where he headed up the ‘Player Acquisition Center of Excellence’ programme.

It was his job to help draw high-profile players to the Middle East in a bid to expand the league’s popularity.

The former Nigeria interrnational now makes a return to England to assist Leicester, but it is believed that Deloitte’s task does not extend to helping blueprint for the sale of the club.

The 2021 FA Cup winners’ owners, the Srivaddhanaprabha family, sought the expertise of Citibank to help them with a prospective sale, putting together a brochure to showcase the club’s assets to send on to investors.

The Foxes were reportedly valued at £200million, although no interested party is thought to have met that figure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Estevao has refused to address reports linking him with a move to Paris Saint-Germain but claims he has received ‘a lot of motivation’ during the international break having struggled for playing time at Chelsea this season.

The 19-year-old has started just one game in the Premier League this season and delivered an impressive performance in Chelsea’s 2-0 win at home to Manchester United on October 31.

However, Estevao was back on the bench for Chelsea’s 1-0 defeat to Sunderland on November 8, although he was brought on as a half-time substitute during the loss at the Stadium of Light.

Xabi Alonso praised Estevao’s response after he was left as an unused substitute during Chelsea’s penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup last month and has insisted that the Brazilian winger ‘will have his moment’ this season.

However, reports have claimed that Estevao has been unhappy with his lack of playing time under Alonso and is considering his future at Chelsea.

Estevao started in both of Brazil’s friendlies during the international break and delivered a lively display during the 7-0 win over Singapore on Tuesday as he scored a goal and registered two assists.

‘I’m very happy to have received the minutes in the friendlies,’ Estevao told ESPN Brasil after his national side’s win at the National Stadium in Singapore.

‘I thank Ancelotti for his confidence because every player wants to play and at Chelsea I’ve had few minutes, but coming here and knowing that the manager trusts me gives me a lot of motivation.

It has been revealed that ESTÊVÃO NO PSG? 🤔🗣️ Com poucos minutos no Chelsea, o atacante da Seleção Brasileira deu uma resposta enigmática quando perguntado sobre uma possível transferência ao Paris Saint-Germain… E aí, fã de esportes, seria uma boa? 👀#FutebolNaESPN #Estêvão #Chelsea #PSG pic.twitter.com/dPQGdVNXWh.

‘We think about ourselves, what we can do better… whether the stadium will be full or not, we think about doing our part so that we can improve.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We know it has been a difficult year because of the World Cup but we highlighted on the pitch that we knew how to respect our opponent in the best way, which is by scoring goals.’.

But when directly asked about a potential move to PSG, Estevao smiled and said: ‘Bye, guys.’.

Chelsea’s next Premier League fixture is at home to Leeds United on Saturday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he rolled out a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

They certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

In a recent development, ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a substantial game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

Recent findings suggest that on the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

It has been revealed that martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring complications to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

According to recent reports, having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

It has been revealed that that Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

It has been revealed that united cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 16:26, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 16:32.

Manchester United have officially confirmed that staff members Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate have left the club alongside Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils made the decision to sack Carrick as head coach last week, and Mauricio Pochettino has since been confirmed as his replacement.

Pochettino officially started work as Man United manager on Wednesday, with the Argentine arriving at Carrington following the completion of his duties with the USA.

Man United have confirmed that Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino have arrived alongside Pochettino.

Meanwhile, five staff members have left alongside Carrick.

"Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian," read a statement from Man United.

"Pochettino’s appointment was declared last Friday with an agreement he’ll begin on 18 November, once he had fulfilled his duties with the US Men’s National Team.

"Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA.

"Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.

"The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

"We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future.".

Man United will continue their Premier League campaign against Liverpool on Sunday afternoon, and Pochettino will be in the dug-out for the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino has taken charge of a team currently down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, picking up only eight points from their first 10 matches of the season.

Liverpool youngster Trey Nyoni has picked out Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard as the ‘toughest opponent’ he has faced at the start of his career.

Odegaard has returned to his sparkling best this season, starting all ten of Arsenal’s opening matches in the Premier League with the reigning champions sitting five points clear at the summit.

Having managed just one goal across the Gunners’ title-winning campaign last term, the 27-year-old appears to have rediscovered his scoring boots, finding the net on five occasions in all competitions this term.

It was Odegaard’s 72nd-minute strike that proved the difference before the international break, when Mikel Arteta’s men were made to work for their victory at home to newly promoted Hull City.

The Norway international will no doubt be desperate to pick up where he left off when the north London giants return to top-flight against at Newcastle on Saturday evening.

Nyoni has himself enjoyed an impressive start to the season at Liverpool and locked horns with Odegaard when the pair did battle at Anfield at the start of the month.

And while Nyoni was taken off before the hour-mark on Merseyside, it’s clear Odegaard left a big impression on the 19-year-old in the 58 minutes his opposite number was on the pitch.

Asked to name the ‘toughest’ player he has come up against, Nyoni told The Inside Scoop, ‘For me personally, I would say Odegaard,’ as he looked back on that afternoon.

‘The way he plays, it’s very busy, moving around and always looking for an option.

‘Nowadays, the idea that if a player isn’t getting goals or assists, they’re useless, but every player has their own role in the team.

‘Odegaard and people like Flo, if they’re not getting goals and assists, people that don’t watch the game automatically think they haven’t played well but that’s not how football works.’.

Mauricio Pochettino has listed the three things he is hoping to bring to Manchester United in his first message to fans.

The Argentine arrived at his latest club on Wednesday, touching down in Manchester immediately after overseeing his final game in charge of the United States.

He led the USMNT to a 2-0 victory over Haiti on Tuesday in Cincinnati, before boarding a flight to England with his trusted assistant Miguel D’Agostino, who will work with him at Old Trafford.

The 54-year-old began work at Carrington on Wednesday, meeting with the players and club hierarchy, as he was pictured with director of football Omar Berrada.

In his first message to United fans, posted to the club’s social media channels, he said: “I am looking forward to meeting you guys.

“I have heard so many good things about you. I hope we bring all the happiness, working together and connect[ion], so that it is going to be a special season, and to make our players fight on the field and get the results we deserve.”.

Pochettino’s first game in charge of United will be a tricky one, as he takes his new side to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday.

He finds the Red Devils mired in the Premier League relegation zone after just one win in 11 matches, a run that saw his predecessor Michael Carrick sacked last Thursday.

Pochettino has plenty of Premier League experience in his managerial career, having overseen Southampton, Totttenham and Chelsea before spells at Paris Saint-Germain and in the United States.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United could push for Villarreal full-back Alex Freeman in January, a player Mauricio Pochettino has tipped to become ‘one of the best in the world’ in his position.

Pochettino was confirmed as Michael Carrick’s successor last week and will arrive in Manchester today ahead of his first game in charge away to Liverpool this weekend.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will be backed in the January transfer window with a striker and a full-back thought to be priorities.

According to recent reports, USA international Folarin Balogun is reportedly a target United are considering to bolster their options up top. The Daily Telegraph report another name has been discussed in Freeman, a player Pochettino is a huge admirer of.

The right-back joined Villarreal in January 2026, thriving under head coach Inigo Perez and emerging as an important member of the first-team. Having started out as a winger, he has established himself at right-back, having also played on the left.

Pochettino recognised the 22-year-old’s qualities while at the helm of the US men’s national team, giving him his senior debut and starting him in four of their five matches at the World Cup.

‘He is so humble, he has an amazing profile, he always listens,’ Pochettino noted after Freeman scored in the USA’s World Cup win over Australia in June.

‘You really enjoy being with him, coaching him, and [he] is an amazing player. For me, [he has potential] to be one of the best players at his position in the world.’.

United have also been linked with another USA international in Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson with former Premier League star Darren Bent believing he and teammate Calvin Bassey would be ‘very good additions’ to United’s backline.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘In January, the first thing Pochettino needs to do as Manchester United manager is go and get defenders,’ Bent told Mr Q.

‘I would say three defenders. A full-back of some kind and two centre-halves, that’s where they need to start. That would be perfect.

Sources indicate that ‘I like the option of Antonee Robinson. I think he’s a very good defender. So that would be a good start because he’s better than what they’ve got right now at Manchester United.’.

Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed the Ukrainian football association for his doping ban.

The Chelsea winger, at the moment on loan at Tottenham, sat out the entirety of the 2025-26 season due to a positive drugs test for meldonium, a banned substance, back in October 2024.

The substance is believed to enhance stamina and respiratory capacity.

The forward was allowed to play once more in the summer, when his four-year ban, that he appealed through the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), was lifted.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso pushed for the winger to go out on loan to earn regular game time, and he reunited with his former boss at Shakhtar Donetsk, Roberto De Zerbi, at Spurs.

Now, Mudryk has pointed the finger at the Ukrainian FA for the ‘adverse finding’ in his out-of-competition sample that was supplied two years ago.

"It was a bolt from the blue,” he noted of his positive drugs test on Ukrainian podcast ‘Guest of Gordon’.

“I couldn’t believe it was true. It was like falling off a skyscraper. In a dream you would hit the ground. In life, I just kept on failing. It hit me very hard, mentally.”.

The 25-year-old claims that he had never heard of meldonium, insisting that there was “no security” on international duty.

Sources indicate that “It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe,” he explained. “It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.”.

Sources indicate that asked how it had got into his system, he replied: "The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team.

“There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games.

Recent findings suggest that “He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup.”.

The winger, who moved to Stamford Bridge in 2023 for an initial £62million - that could rise to £89m - was asked point-blank if he blamed his national setup.

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway.

Mudryk has played just once for Spurs since his comeback from his ban, having picked up what De Zerbi classed as a “stupid” ankle injury in training after his debut off the bench against Nottingham Forest.

He is hoped to be back this weekend for Spurs’ home game against Ipswich.

Ashley Young reckons it is time for Manchester United to move on from Bruno Fernandes and feels there is a Premier League star who should be signed to replace him.

Fernandes has consistently been the Red Devils’ best player since joining from Sporting in January 2020.

However, at 32 years old and with upcoming manager Mauricio Pochettino arriving this week, doubts over whether Fernandes will remain the focal point of the team are being raised.

The United captain is into the final few months of his contract and has reportedly rejected two offers of a new deal.

The club has the option to extend his current contract by another month, which would prevent Fernandes leaving on a free transfer in the summer, but he could still be sold in 2027 if that option is taken up.

Former Red Devils man Young reckons it is time to move on from Fernandes and thinks the man to replace him is Nottingham Forest and England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

The former Wolves star turns 27 in January and Young feels now is the time for Manchester United to make him their main man, replacing Fernandes.

In a recent development, ‘He’s been unbelievable for the club, the standout performer,’ Young noted of Fernandes on Overlap Daily. ‘But there’s been so much that’s come about. He’s turned down another contract, we’re hearing.

‘You want to build around a player. He’s 33 next year. Age is nothing but a number, but he’s not in his peak. I wouldn’t say past it, but he’s getting older now.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘For me, I would go and sign Morgan Gibbs-White. I’m just throwing that name out there. But you’re thinking a number 10 and you want to build a team around a player.

In a recent development, ‘He’s young, he’s hungry, he’s just got in the England squad. I think he’s got the capabilities to go and play for – no disrespect to Nottingham Forest – a bigger club. And I think he’s someone that Manchester United need, in his peak years.

‘I think he’s shown more than enough at Nottingham Forest to be able to go and say I can play for a bigger club like Manchester United and take the weight of that.’.

As much as signing latest players will be on the agenda for the new Manchester United manager, getting rid of unwanted squad members may be the bigger test.

Gary Neville feels there needs to be a significant cull over the next few transfer windows, with some significant names ideally being axed at the end of the season.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If you look through it now I’d say Martinez would go, [Matthijs] De Ligt would go, [Noussair] Mazraoui would go, [Mason] Mount would go, first wave next summer. [Marcus] Rashford if you can, and [Joshua] Zirkzee,’ the former full-back remarked on Stick to United.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at [Luke] Shaw, [Harry] Maguire, [Diogo] Dalot, Bruno [Fernandes], that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on [Carlos] Baleba and [Andrey] Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’.

Mykhailo Mudryk has revealed that Xabi Alonso personally persuaded him to leave Chelsea on loan.

The Ukrainian, who returned from a drugs ban for meldonium in the summer, joined Tottenham in a Deadline Day switch that saw him reunite with his former manager Roberto De Zerbi, who coached him at Skakhtar Donetsk.

The winger was the subject of much Premier League interest when it came apparent that he was available for a temporary move, and he revealed on Ukrainian podcast ‘Guest of Gordon’ that Brighton, Brentford and Leeds all registered their interest in him.

Instead, he chose to move to the north of the capital, where he has made just one appearance before being struck down with an ankle injury he picked up in training.

Speaking of his move to Spurs, Mudryk said that Chelsea boss Alonso “told me straight up to my face: ‘You had better go and play and get some minutes then come back. I am counting on you.’".

The 25-year-old made his highly-anticipated Spurs debut against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground in September, but he has been sidelined since then with an matter that De Zerbi said was “stupid”.

He is expected to return to action this weekend when the north Londoners take on newly-promoted Ipswich Town at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, coming off the back of a run of three wins in their last four games.

Spurs’ recent resurgence was dealt an abrupt end by Leeds at Elland Road before the recent international break, with a Noah Okafor goal on 79 minutes the difference in Yorkshire to snap De Zerbi’s three-game winning streak.

Manchester United have identified three potential defensive signings for Mauricio Pochettino in the January transfer window, according to reports.

Pochettino arrived at United’s training ground on Wednesday afternoon to begin his stint as head coach following the decision to sack Michael Carrick last week.

United have faced criticism over their transfer activity in the summer as they spent £155 million on signing three midfielders in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.

Pochettino now arrives at Old Trafford short of options with striker Benjamin Sesko sidelined until next year with a shin injury, while Luke Shaw has missed United’s last seven fixtures.

According to Sky Sports, United are willing to bolster Pochettino’s squad in the January window and the club will consult the Argentine over any potential signings.

The report claims that Everton centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite and Fulham’s Calvin Bassey are two players who United are considering for January.

United had two bids rejected for Branthwaite in 2024, including an offer of £50 million, and held talks with the defender’s representatives earlier this year.

The report adds that Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson is also one of United’s options and the 29-year-old has already played under Pochettino with the United States national team.

Elsewhere, reports in Spain claim that Barcelona left-back Alejandro Balde is open to a move to United in the upcoming transfer window.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 22:54 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 22:55 EST, 15 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued on Sunday night with a pitstop at an NFL showdown.

The manager has one game left in charge of the United States before parting ways with the national team to join Manchester United after agreeing a deal with the Premier League club earlier this week.

The Argentine will replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Sources indicate that before his return to England, the 54-year-old is enjoying his swansong with the US. In between overseeing his final games in charge of the national team, Pochettino was spotted soaking in the action of the other variety of football.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss attended the primetime NFL showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio on Sunday night.

The head coach, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead of the Sunday Night Football matchup.

USMNT and future Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is at the Bengals-Steelers game 😭🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/B7Irn0YLnd.

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued at the NFL on Sunday night.

The newly introduced Manchester United boss attended the Cincinnati Bengals' game at Paycor Stadium.

He was greeted by kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow - members of the Bengals' special teams - on the turf before kickoff.

The US is set to face Haiti in the second-leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

The game, which will take place around a mile north of the Bengals' Paycor Stadium, will mark Pochettino's final match in charge of the US national team.

He also took charge of the USA's 6-0 first-leg win against Haiti on Tuesday, which marked the first stop on his farewell tour.

Sources indicate that pochettino will begin his newly introduced role with Manchester United on Wednesday, immediately following Tuesday's second-leg. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday.

He emotionally addressed his departure from the US setup and impending newly introduced job in a press conference on Friday.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

The Argentine was captured on the sidelines ahead of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

According to recent reports, ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

According to recent reports, ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 16:56.

Manchester United could reportedly sign Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde on loan during the January transfer window without having to pay his full wages.

Balde's future remains the subject of much speculation, with the Spain international expected to leave the Catalan outfit when the winter market opens for business.

Man United were linked with the left-back over the summer but were ultimately unable to progress due to the 23-year-old's desire to remain at Camp Nou.

It has been a frustrating campaign for Balde, who has been restricted to just five appearances for Barcelona, and he has not started a single game at club level this term.

The defender has allegedly accepted that he will need to leave Barcelona in January for the sake of his career, and Man United are desperate to bring in a left-back.

According to RAC, Barcelona are keen to move Balde on in January in order to free up space for them to sign a centre-back.

The report claims that the La Liga champions would prefer a permanent exit, but a loan deal is also possible, with Man United not even needing to cover his full wage packet.

A partial wage contribution could potentially be accepted by Barcelona providing that enough space in their budget is made to bring in a new player.

Balde has made 173 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions, scoring three goals and registering 21 assists in the process.

#37339. Open up peer review to early-career researchers

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1077 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Open up peer review to early-career researchers

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1077 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Co-reviewing initiatives provide structured pathways for early-career researchers to become peer reviewers.
  • Early-career researchers power science’s engine room and yet they make up a small fraction of peer reviewers.
  • Sources indicate that although senior researchers can provide knowledge of the bigger-picture, ECRs are often closer to the latest techniques for practical experiments and analysing data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Co-reviewing initiatives provide structured pathways for early-career researchers to become peer reviewers. Credit: Getty.

Early-career researchers power science’s engine room and yet they make up a small fraction of peer reviewers. When they are involved in reviewing, their contributions are not always recognized. In some cases, they do the work, but their senior colleagues take the credit. This is not acceptable and the Nature Portfolio journals are working to change it. Researchers at all career stages should have the opportunity to be peer reviewers — especially early-career researchers (ECRs). Now, the first large-scale analysis of the Nature Portfolio Early Career Researcher Co-Review programme reveals the benefits, for researchers and science.

Sources indicate that although senior researchers can provide knowledge of the bigger-picture, ECRs are often closer to the latest techniques for practical experiments and analysing data. They also tend to be more up to date with rapidly changing technologies. Involving ECRs in the peer-review process gives them a necessary voice that can help to shape the scientific record.

At the start of 2025, Nature joined Nature Portfolio’s ECR Co-Review programme (see Nature 641, 560; 2025). This initiative, which began with Nature Reviews journals and later Nature Communications, invites established reviewers to involve an ECR in the process, while retaining responsibility for the final review. Journal editors also provide training to participating ECRs and those who have taken part in co-reviewing are then offered the opportunity to review studies on their own.

The Nature Portfolio analysis finds that the programme is increasing the representation of ECRs among peer reviewers and is helping to bridge the gender gap in research.

Recent findings suggest that overall, ECRs accounted for 17% of reviewers at Nature and 11% at Nature Communications. The analysis is based on data from 78,661 reviewers and 24,645 research manuscripts submitted to Nature Communications (between 1 April 2024 and 31 July 2025) and to Nature (between 1 February 2025 and 31 July 2025).

Nature project to encourage early-career researchers in peer review is working.

Nature project to encourage early-career researchers in peer review is working.

In a recent development, more than one-quarter of manuscripts at both journals had at least one reviewer who was a PhD candidate or postdoctoral researcher. Women accounted for around 40% of ECR reviewers compared with 24% of established researchers.

In a survey of around 2,500 established researchers and 2,400 ECRs who participated in the co-review programme, 88% of established researchers remarked they are more likely to agree to review a manuscript if they can co-review with an ECR. Nearly all of the ECR respondents rated the initiative as an ‘excellent’ or ‘good’ way to involve ECRs and to improve transparency in peer review. Many respondents also reported that they thought participation of ECRs sped up the turnaround times for reviews.

These are promising results, although the analysis also highlights areas in which more progress is needed, such as the inclusion of reviewers from a wider range of countries. Researchers affiliated with the United States made up the largest share of ECR reviewers on both journals: around 42% at Nature Communications and 49% at Nature. The overwhelming majority of the remaining reviewers were also from high-income countries.

Nature Portfolio journals are not alone in creating structured pathways for ECRs to become peer reviewers. Several other publishers have developed initiatives that combine mentoring, training and formal recognition for ECRs.

Industry observers note that for the past 15 years, EMBO Press, which publishes five journals including The EMBO Journal and EMBO Reports, has encouraged established researchers to co-review manuscripts with postdocs in their laboratories, while requiring that co-reviewers are recognized. In 2024, EMBO Press, which is run by the European Molecular Biology Organization (EMBO), debuted an initiative inviting ECRs with at least two years of postdoc experience to participate in peer reviews on their own. The publisher has been monitoring uptake of the programme and a representative told Nature that the quality of ECR review reports match those of reviews completed by established referees.

Junior researchers are losing out by ghostwriting peer reviews.

Junior researchers are losing out by ghostwriting peer reviews.

In September, the journal FEBS Open Bio (published by Wiley on behalf of the Federation of European Biochemical Societies) launched an effort called the Early Career Reviewer Hub that helps PhD students and postdocs to gain peer-review experience in molecular sciences. Participants in the initiative receive training from the journal’s editors and must nominate established researchers to mentor them. The ECRs review articles known as Research Protocols, which detail experimental procedures. There are other initiatives, too — a positive sign that the publishing community is doing more to involve ECRs in the peer-review process.

Sources indicate that peer review is fundamental to research and provides a way to rigorously evaluate science. It is a process through which researchers learn how to assess their colleagues’ work and, at the same time, learn about how their own articles will be assessed.

However, the current peer-review system is stretched and scientists face ever-increasing demands on their time. Publishers need to ensure that more ECRs have the opportunity to contribute to this key service and that they are recognized for their work. Peer reviewers must reflect the true diversity of research itself.

‘Why did they spend £50m on Santos?’ Ince told The Sun. ‘That’s £50m wasted. They could have put that into the defence or bought a striker.

Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi is targeting a move outside of the Premier League despite interest from Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham, according to reports.

Kroupi joined Bournemouth in a £12 million deal from French side Lorient last year and scored 13 goals in his first season in the Premier League.

The 20-year-old has suffered a disrupted start to the new campaign as he required surgery on a foot injury sustained during a pre-season training session in Austria in July.

Kroupi returned in Bournemouth’s 3-0 win away to Manchester United on October 25 and has made three more appearances as a substitute for Marco Rose’s side.

During the international break, Kroupi was handed his senior debut for France as he featured in the 3-1 defeat to Italy, as well as in the 2-1 win over Turkey.

The French striker has attracted interest from Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham, while Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Barcelona have also been monitoring his progress in the Premier League.

However, David Ornstein has claimed that Kroupi will look to move overseas when he leaves Bournemouth, although the club are not looking to sell the forward in the January transfer window.

‘There was a substantial story recently about Alex Scott possibly leaving in the January transfer window, that was conditional on Bournemouth receiving £100 million and being in a really strong position in the Premier League where that becomes a bit of a no-brainer because in six months’ time he’ll have a year to go on his contract and it’s a very different conversation,’ Ornstein stated on The Athletic FC’s podcast.

‘Kroupi has got much longer on his contract for a start, so there’s no massive need to sell in a way you would consider selling Scott.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 18 Nov 2026 17:17.

Barnsley will welcome Sheffield Wednesday to Oakwell on Friday for a South Yorkshire Derby of major importance at both ends of the League One table.

The visitors moved up to fifth spot with a return to winning ways under new management last weekend, while their visitors sit 23rd in the midst of a winless run in the third tier.

Barnsley head into a South Yorkshire Derby on Friday aiming to end a poor run of League One form and climb towards safety.

From their 13 league matches so far this season, since the summer return of former promotion-winning manager Daniel Stendel, they have picked up just nine points, winning just two and losing eight of those.

The most recent of those victories came at the beginning of September, and the Reds have gone winless in nine third-tier matches since, having gone into a meeting with fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic last weekend with fresh optimism on the back of a draw against Oxford United and consecutive cup victories.

They failed to convert those results into an elusive league win, though, leaving the Brick Community Stadium empty-handed following a 2-1 defeat, as Cameron McGeehan cancelled Fraser Murray's opener out on the hour mark, only for Jensen Weir to put the hosts back ahead 15 minutes from time.

Now three points adrift of safety and only above basement side Bromley on goal difference, Barnsley will be desperate to begin reversing their fortunes with a win over their rivals on Friday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the short trip aiming to make it consecutive league victories under newly introduced management to climb closer to the top two.

After a positive start to life back in League One, with fresh ownership, a newly introduced and improved squad and their sights set on a return to the Championship, Sheffield Wednesday hit a tougher spell across October and early November with consecutive losses spelling the end of Henrik Pedersen's tenure.

Consecutive draws then followed under caretaker management, leaving the Owls on 20 points from 13 games after a fast start, before they turned to newly introduced manager Dave Challinor, whose tenure started with consecutive cup defeats at the hands of fourth-tier Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley.

Saturday then brought about a first league game as Owls boss for Challinor, and he oversaw a first victory at Hillsborough in style as the South Yorkshire outfit leapfrogged their visitors with a 3-0 triumph thanks to Billy Mitchell's opener and goals from Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard in the final 10 minutes.

Now hoping to be out of their brief slump and with fresh optimism under their latest boss, Sheffield Wednesday find themselves fifth and six points off the automatic promotion places and will bid to keep building momentum with a second straight win on Friday.

Barnsley form (all competitions):.

Sheffield Wednesday League One form:.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):.

Barnsley remain without defender Jack Shepherd, while key midfielder and captain Cameron McGeehan is also out suspended after reaching five yellow cards for the season last time out.

Fabio Jalo and Ben Hamed Toure are out injured, while Patrick Kelly is back in contention after being away on international duty and will come back into the midfield.

Kelly will replace McGeehan and could join Luca Connell and Daniel Johnson in the midfield, while Reyes Cleary and Vimal Yoganathan will again support a lone striker with Makenzie Kirk, Rylan Brownlie and Amani Richards competing to lead the line.

Sheffield Wednesday may be unchanged from last week's impressive 3-0 victory, having seen their injury troubles eased recently with Liam Cooper, Bernard, Mitchell, first-choice goalkeeper Joe Lumley and danger man Louie Barry all back available.

Ali Al-Hamadi, Kieran Morrison and Jordi Liongola are also in contention, with Mason Burstow still out, while Barry may be eased back in after a long layoff with Barry Bannan and Callum Slattery likely to continue supporting front man Keillor-Dunn, who has scored in each of his last three appearances.

Elsewhere, Bernard and Cooper should again be joined by Sil Swinkels in a back three, while they are light on the left-hand side with Reece James and Max Lowe out of action alongside Burstow.

Barnsley possible starting lineup:.

Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche; Johnson, Connell; Yoganathan, Kelly, Cleary; Kirk.

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:.

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Valery, Heskey, Mitchell, Gray; Slattery, Bannan; Keillor-Dunn.

Sheffield Wednesday looked somewhat back to their best in last weekend's beating of fellow promotion-chasers Plymouth Argyle, and we fancy them to make it consecutive clean sheets and wins against a Barnsley side devoid of confidence and without top scorer McGeehan.

Barcelona have confirmed they have no plans to sell Alejandro Balde and insist the Manchester United-linked left-back remains an ‘crucial player’ for the club going forward.

Balde has been with Barca since the age of just eight, making a total of 173 appearances in all competitions since breaking into the first-team squad back in 2021.

In that time, the 23-year-old has helped the Catalan giants win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles – the most recent coming under Hansi Flick last season.

However, Balde has become an increasingly peripheral figure at the Camp Nou in recent months, with all five of his appearances this term coming from the substitutes bench.

Balde at the moment finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at Barca and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, this has forced Balde to consider his options and the full-back is understood to be keen on joining Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United in January.

Other reports suggest that ‘everything Balde has heard about his situation has come through press conferences’ and the defender views the Premier League as a possible escape route.

The subject of Balde’s future has proven a major talking point both in the media and amongst Barcelona’s fanbase – and the topic was raised during Catalunya Radio’s joint interview with club chiefs Bojan and Deco on Wednesday.

Asked about the possible sale of Balde this winter, football coordinator Bojan replied: ‘Balde is a fantastic lad.

‘Obviously, he’s in an uncomfortable situation. The player wants to play.

Deco, Barca’s sporting director, was similarly unequivocal when asked if a transfer deal could be on the cards for Balde.

‘No,’ the ex-Barca, Chelsea and Portugal responded.

‘There is also the player’s side, but he hasn’t told us anything about being unhappy, that’s not the case.’.

Diogo Dalot was therefore forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back in the bleak final weeks of Michael Carrick’s tenure at the Theatre of Dreams.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel had stated he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Sources indicate that he needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

Proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’.

Sources indicate that something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

Recent findings suggest that and then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

Sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller.

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback.

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead.

Yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

Sources indicate that spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

In a recent development, england had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

Recent findings suggest that england ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

Industry observers note that spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

It has been revealed that spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

In a recent development, pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

Industry observers note that england got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move.

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot.

The referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

Sources indicate that there were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

Eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

According to recent reports, four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

Kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded.

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net.

But then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

The atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

It has been revealed that now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

Spain threw everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

Frank Lampard appears to have endorsed Chelsea’s pursuit of Alex Scott while revealing his ‘love’ for the ‘quality’ Bournemouth and England midfielder.

Though he picked up a thigh injury while on international duty with England last month, Scott’s outstanding performance in the Three Lions’ thumping 7-0 win over Croatia did little to quieten rumours of a potential significant-money move.

Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham have all been credited with an interest in recent weeks and months, but Chelsea reportedly find themselves in pole position to land Scott this winter.

The Blues are actively scouring the market for midfield reinforcements after failing to bring in a replacement for Enzo Fernandez in the summer and are said to be ‘increasingly confident’ of reaching an agreement for Scott.

Up until this point, Bournemouth have publicly played down speculation that Scott could be on the move, especially midway through the campaign when they risk derailing the side’s encouraging progress under Marco Rose.

However, it’s understood an offer in region of £100million could be enough to convince the Cherries into selling Scott in what would undoubtedly be one of this January’s biggest deals.

One man who knows more than anyone what it takes to thrive in Chelsea’s midfield is Lampard, arguably the club’s greatest ever player, who won 14 trophies across an illustrious 13-year career at Stamford Bridge.

During a wide-ranging interview on the Rio Ferdinand Presents YouTube channel, Lampard made it clear just how highly he rated Scott when he was asked to name his dream Premier League midfield three on current form.

‘I love Alex Scott at Bournemouth, I think he’s quality.

‘It’s fine and Declan will just shrug it off.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Strasbourg have confirmed the appointment of Vitor Matos as their new head coach following the sacking of Hugo Oliveira during the international break.

Matos arrives from Championship side Swansea City, just four months after agreeing a contract until 2030 with the Welsh side.

The 38-year-old joined Swansea from Maritimo in November last year to succeed Alan Sheehan, taking over when the Welsh club were languishing down in 20th.

He led Swansea to an 11th-place finish in 2025-26, and they have started strongly in the Championship this term, sitting sixth in the table and just three points off the top.

But Swansea's hopes of a return to the Premier League for the first time since 2017-18 will now rest on another boss.

Former Swansea captain Ashley Williams is set to return to the club to join an interim coaching team also featuring fellow ex-players Kristian O'Leary and Leon Britton.

Welcome, Vitor! Vitor Matos has been named the Club’s upcoming head coach https://t.co/QKD6FJpEgP.

— Racing Club de Strasbourg Alsace English (@RCSA_English) November 18, 2026.

Matos took charge of 47 matches across all competitions with Swansea, winning 22 (D7 L18), and he arrives at a Strasbourg side struggling in Ligue 1 so far.

Following a 3-1 defeat to Toulouse on November 6, Strasbourg have suffered six league defeats in 2026-27, their second-highest total after 10 matches of a top-flight season in the 21st century, behind only 2020-21 (eight – they finished 15th that season).

They have also lost five of their last six Ligue 1 matches (W1), as many defeats as they suffered in their first 22 games in 2026 (W10 D7), leaving them 13th in the table.

Matos does not have to wait long for his first home game in charge of the Ligue 1 side, with Brest the visitors to the Stade de la Meinau on Saturday.

Latest Update: Hansi Flick finds unexpected Frenkie De Jong solution

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (932 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 17:18, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 17:29.
  • Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick may have found an unexpected way to accommodate Frenkie de Jong in his increasingly competitive squad, with the Netherlands international demonstrating his value in an unfamiliar position during the club's recent victory over Atletico Madrid.
  • The 29-year-old has endured another injury-disrupted year, while the arrival of Rodri has added further competition to a midfield already featuring Pedri, Gavi, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 17:18, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 17:29.

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick may have found an unexpected way to accommodate Frenkie de Jong in his increasingly competitive squad, with the Netherlands international demonstrating his value in an unfamiliar position during the club's recent victory over Atletico Madrid.

The 29-year-old has endured another injury-disrupted year, while the arrival of Rodri has added further competition to a midfield already featuring Pedri, Gavi, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Dani Olmo.

Yet De Jong's performance in Barcelona's 2-1 comeback victory over Atletico on November 8 offered a reminder of why Flick continues to regard him as an key member of his squad.

Introduced at half-time with Barcelona trailing, the Dutchman was surprisingly deployed at right-back rather than in his customary midfield role.

The decision helped Barcelona gain control of possession and establish a stronger presence in the opposition half, with De Jong eventually returning to central midfield following another tactical adjustment.

His influence was reflected in the statistics: he completed 65 of his 67 passes, achieving an accuracy rate of 97%, despite playing only 45 minutes.

For a player who has repeatedly faced questions about his future at the Camp Nou, it was another example of how his particular qualities can provide solutions beyond the position traditionally associated with him.

Flick's decision to introduce De Jong at right-back was particularly significant given Barcelona's difficulties in controlling the first half against Diego Simeone's side.

The German manager replaced Brian Farinas with the former Ajax midfielder, who offered a very different interpretation of the position.

Rather than remaining close to the touchline, De Jong frequently moved into central areas when Barcelona had possession, helping his teammates progress the ball through Atletico's pressure.

His ability to receive under pressure, turn away from opponents and carry possession forward allowed Barcelona to build attacks without relying exclusively on passes from their defenders.

That mobility has been one of De Jong's defining qualities throughout his career, although his contribution does not always translate into goals or assists.

According to Mundo Deportivo, he completed 22 passes in the attacking third against Atletico, more than any other Barcelona player, despite spending the entire first half on the bench.

Barcelona's overall possession increased from 58% before the interval to 68% in the second half, during which they registered 10 attempts on goal and allowed just two.

Those improvements cannot be attributed solely to De Jong, but his introduction provided a technical outlet that had been missing earlier in the contest.

Flick subsequently moved the Dutchman back into midfield after Eric Garcia entered the match, illustrating another advantage of having a player comfortable in several positions.

De Jong has previously been used as a central defender and in more advanced midfield roles, while his experience in Barcelona's build-up play makes him particularly effective when moving between the defensive and midfield lines.

The Atletico performance offered further evidence that his versatility can be valuable even when he is not an automatic starter in his preferred position.

De Jong's situation has changed considerably since the summer of 2022, when Manchester United pursued his signature under former Ajax manager Erik ten Hag.

Barcelona were prepared to consider his departure during a period of significant financial difficulties, but the midfielder remained determined to continue his career in Catalonia.

His relationship with the club has subsequently been complicated by questions over deferred wages, recurring injuries and speculation surrounding his importance to successive managers.

Nevertheless, Barcelona demonstrated their commitment to the Dutchman by extending his contract until June 2029 in October last year.

The renewal came despite his difficult injury history, which included the ankle problems that ruled him out of Euro 2024.

He suffered another major setback during the 2026 World Cup, sustaining a knee ligament injury that prevented him from featuring during the opening months of the current campaign.

De Jong eventually returned against Real Madrid on October 25 and recently reached 300 competitive appearances for Barcelona.

However, the arrival of Rodri has created an additional selection challenge for Flick.

The Spanish international offers a more natural defensive presence at the base of midfield, while Pedri remains central to Barcelona's ability to dictate possession and create opportunities.

Gavi, Bernal, Fermin and Olmo provide further alternatives, leaving Flick with considerable flexibility but difficult decisions whenever his midfielders are fit.

De Jong's capacity to operate in several roles could therefore prove particularly useful, especially when Barcelona need additional composure during the early stages of their attacking moves.

His ability to advance with the ball also offers something different from Rodri's positional discipline and Pedri's creativity between the lines.

That does not necessarily mean De Jong will become a regular right-back. His appearance against Atletico was a tactical response to the circumstances of a particular match rather than confirmation of a permanent positional change.

There is also the continuing question of his fitness.

De Jong withdrew from the Netherlands squad during the November international break after experiencing muscular discomfort, although Barcelona subsequently confirmed that the problem was not serious.

The midfielder is expected to be available for Sunday's La Liga encounter with Villarreal, providing Flick with another vital option as Rodri continues his recovery from a hamstring injury.

After years in which De Jong was frequently discussed as a potential departure, his recent performances have underlined why Barcelona have been reluctant to give up on him.

His future role may depend less on securing one fixed position in Flick's midfield than on his ability to perform several functions within the same game.

It has been revealed that the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

According to recent reports, if you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

It has been revealed that “He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

US loses measles elimination status: what it means for the world

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1032 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Measles has taken off in US states such as South Carolina, prompting health officials to increase vaccination campaigns.Credit: Sean Rayford/Getty.
  • Measles is officially back in the United States.
  • The United States managed to eliminate measles in 2000 thanks to an intensive vaccination campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Measles has taken off in US states such as South Carolina, prompting health officials to increase vaccination campaigns.Credit: Sean Rayford/Getty.

Measles is officially back in the United States. Today, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) announced that the United States has lost its measles elimination status because of an outbreak that has caused more than 5,700 infections and 10 deaths this year, the deadliest such episode in more than three decades (see ‘Measles unleashed’). Measles has also been re-established in Mexico and Bolivia, PAHO determined.

The United States managed to eliminate measles in 2000 thanks to an intensive vaccination campaign. But declining vaccination rates mean that parts of the population became susceptible to the infection in the past few years, notes virologist Paul Offit, the director of the Vaccine Education Center at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia in Pennsylvania. “We’ve taken an enormous step back in public health,” Offit says.

Source: International Vaccine Access Center, Johns Hopkins University.

It has been revealed that measles — a viral infection that causes fever and a rash and can lead to potentially fatal brain complications — is one of the world’s most contagious diseases, and its resurgence in the United States could have global consequences, states Jennifer Nuzzo, an epidemiologist and director of the Pandemic Center at Brown University in Providence, Rhode Island. “Having measles return to any country increases the likelihood that other countries will see an increase in measles.”.

PAHO determines that a country has lost its measles elimination status if one genetic variant of the virus is continuously transmitted there for 12 months or more. Genetic data help to distinguish between a single persistent chain of transmission and various shorter, unrelated outbreaks, which could be triggered by imported cases. In the United States, Bolivia and Mexico, data highlighted prolonged transmission of a single genotype of measles, suggesting that the virus has become entrenched in these countries.

Industry observers note that as of 13 November, there were 58,213 confirmed measles cases in the Americas in 2026, compared with 12,596 cases during the same period in 2025. “The current situation requires urgent attention,” Jarbas Barbosa, PAHO’s director, said at the announcement today.

The current outbreak also has some features that make it especially concerning.

Whereas measles is typically seen as a childhood disease, around 40% of US measles cases this year were in people aged 20 and older. In Pennsylvania, the state with the highest number of cases, two-thirds of measles infections have been in adults. “We’re seeing a different kind of epidemiology,” Offit says, adding that adults are more likely to have serious complications than all but the youngest children.

Recent findings suggest that before measles vaccines became available in the 1960s, most children got infected and developed immunity to the virus. As a result, cases in adults were very rare. But young adults “who grew up at a time when measles wasn’t circulating in this country ... were never naturally infected,” Offit states. If they weren’t vaccinated as children, they are now vulnerable to the virus.

154 million lives and counting: 5 charts reveal the power of vaccines.

154 million lives and counting: 5 charts reveal the power of vaccines.

Recent findings suggest that that pool of unprotected people, combined with declining vaccination rates, explains why more adults are vulnerable now than in the past. Offit notes that, in Pennsylvania, certain traditional Christian groups such as the Amish and Mennonite communities typically do not vaccinate their children. In the past, people in these groups were unlikely to catch measles because high vaccination rates in the surrounding communities suppressed viral spread. That is no longer the case.

Recent findings suggest that physicians are also starting to see something that has been very rare in the United States in the last few decades: congenital measles. In this case a baby is born with an active infection because of transmission from an infected mother. There have been six cases this year in Pennsylvania alone.

“We have a whole generation of women of reproductive age who were never vaccinated” because of falling vaccination rates, says Neil Silverman, who specialises in maternal and fetal medicine with a focus on infectious disease, at the University of California Los Angeles.

Measles raises the risk that pregnant people will develop pneumonia, which can lead to hospitalization and even intensive-care admission. Severe cases can lead to pregnancy loss and preterm birth. In Pennsylvania, almost 100 cases of measles have been reported in pregnant people this year.

It has been revealed that because measles is so contagious, it’s the first one to come back when vaccination rates drop, researchers say. But others might follow.

“If people are not getting vaccinated against measles, that means they’re also not getting vaccinated against mumps and rubella,” notes Silverman, because in the United States, vaccines against all three diseases are given in a single combination jab, the ‘MMR’ vaccine. “We’re already starting to see mumps outbreaks scattered across the country,” he says.
